quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Talk to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so the motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down earlier, and increase your following distance. Always warn your passenger about hazards ahead.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately. Do not brake while swerving, as this may cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. They also provide extra protection in a crash.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, group riders should:

options.text: Ride on the far right of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation normally, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
Either the left or right side

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, cover the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or with their turn signals. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When turning:

options.text: You can safely use both brakes if you do it correctly.
Braking feels the same as on a straight road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can safely use both brakes if you do it correctly.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes to stop quickly while turning, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Helps protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants when riding in hot weather. They protect you from injuries and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: Normally, you should stay how far behind the vehicle in front of you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle in front of you. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this distance.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older is legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while under the influence is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If you brake while turning a curve:

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean.
You may have less grip as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When your motorcycle leans, some of your tire grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down and approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it. Then speed up and leave it behind. If you see a larger animal, slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has curved mirrors and you are not used to them, you should practice because:

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make things look farther away than they really are.
They make things look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make things look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. But they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has curved ones.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars to avoid the center. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should:

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Not need hearing protection if they wear a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing while still allowing you to hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually as powerful as car headlights.
Usually less powerful than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane when riding in traffic. Swerving to avoid a small animal could cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: When it is raining, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars has not washed away yet. Riding in tire tracks left by cars is safest. The left tire track is usually your best choice.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can prevent drunk driving by arranging other transportation, involving them in other activities, using excuses to keep them from leaving, and getting other friends to help. Never tell them to drive on less-crowded roads.
